Date August 28, 19 39.
Subject. Information re Zang Nyoh-tsing (常玉清) and his reported death
in Nanking.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by C [签名]

The press reports of August 21, 1939, to the
effect that Zang Nyoh-tsing was recently assassinated
in Nanking, are groundless according to independent
information.

Zang is reported to have arrived, in company
of several friends, at the Kiangwan Aerodrome on
August 18 and to have stayed in the New Asia Hotel,
Tiendong Road, during his sojourn here. Although he
is nominally counsellor to the Reformed Government,
he actually discharges the duties of a Commander-in-
Chief of the Japanese-sponsored Guerilla Units in
Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Provinces.

Zang was the chairman of the Huang Dao Associa-
tion (in the New Asia Hotel, Tiendong Road) which was
later renamed the An Ching League (安清全盟会) and
removed to Nanking during the latter part of 1938.
The Huang Dao Association was notorious for its
terroristic activities in Shanghai, but since its re-
organization into the An Tsing League, its activities
have been chiefly confined to the establishment of
connections with members of the "Green Pang", which,
however, have not been very successful. Zang is
illiterate and has no political knowledge. He remains
as the Chairman of the An Tsing League which is doing
little or nothing, but has not been abolished by the
Japanese authorities simply because of Zang's loyalty
which deters them from discarding him.

主题：关于常玉清（Zang Nyoh-tsing）及其据报在南京死亡的情报。
由督察顾宝华（Kuh Pao-hwa）制作 转呈者 C [签名]

根据独立情报，1939年8月21日新闻界关于常玉清近期在南京被暗杀的报道毫无根据。

据报，常于8月18日在数名朋友的陪同下抵达江湾机场，并在其逗留上海期间入住天潼路新亚酒店。虽然他名义上是维新政府的顾问，但实际上履行着日本赞助的苏浙皖三省游击队总司令的职责。

常曾是黄道协会（位于天潼路新亚酒店）的主席，该协会后更名为安清全盟会，并于1938年下半年迁往南京。黄道协会因在上海的恐怖活动而臭名昭著，但自改组为安清联盟以来，其活动主要局限于与“青帮”成员建立联系，然而成效甚微。常是文盲，没有政治知识。他仍然担任安清联盟主席，该组织几乎无所作为，但日本当局并未将其取缔，仅仅是因为常的忠诚使他们不愿抛弃他。

Chinese-American Daily News and Ta Ying Yeh Pao (21/8) :- 22.8.39 (PM)

DEATH OF ZANG NYOH-CHING CONFIRMED : HWANG DAO ASSOCIATION
DISSOLVED : REHABILITATION SOCIETY APPEARS IN HONGKEW

It is not confirmed Zang Nyoh-ching
(常之清), spy and terroristic chief of the Hwang Dao
Association, was assassinated by patriotic elements in
Nanking. As no one connected with the Association is
regarded to be of use to the Japanese, the Association is
now in a state of dissolution.
Originally, Zang was in Shanghai but later
as he became notorious, he left for Nanking. He established
an office on Jessfield Road, Shanghai, which now no more
exists. It is learned, however, that a certain party has
organized a "Rehabilitation Society" (復兴社) to take
the place of the Hwang Dao Association and which is managed
by one Chu (朱). Its members are mostly loafers, refugees,
and persons of Shanghai's lower orders. They are enrolled
on the pretext of serving as cotton mill workers with a
daily wages of 30 cents. The person in charge of the
Society was once arrested by the Police authorities and is
now living in hiding, though somewhat actively in Hongkew.

《中美日报》和《大英夜报》（8月21日）:- 1939年8月22日（下午）

确认常之清死亡：黄道协会解散：复兴社出现在虹口

据证实，黄道协会的间谍兼恐怖头目常之清（Zang Nyoh-ching）在南京被爱国人士暗杀。由于与该协会有关的人员均被认为对日本人无用，该协会目前处于解散状态。
起初，常在上海，但后来因声名狼藉而前往南京。他在上海极司菲尔路设立了一个办事处，但该办事处现已不复存在。然而据悉，某方已组织了一个“复兴社”以取代黄道协会，由一名姓朱的人管理。其成员多为游手好闲者、难民和上海下层社会人员。他们以充当棉纺厂工人、日薪30分为名被招募。该社负责人曾被警方逮捕，目前虽在虹口 somewhat 活跃，但正躲藏中。

CHINA PRESS.

“Kingly Way”
Leader Said
Assassinated

“Two Ton” Zang Shot
Down At Banquet,
Shanghai Told

“Two Ton” Zang Yu-ching, one-time leader of the local terrorist tribe north of Soochow Creek, is said to be dead.
Reports received in local semi-official circles yesterday are to the effect that “Two Ton” was shot to death by assassins at Nanking three days ago.
The assassins, said to have been seven in number, crashed a banquet at Nanking being given by Zang.
Military Mausers started spitting death and when the smoke had cleared away, “Two Ton” lay stretched on the floor, the major casualty of the incident. “Two Ton” died on the spot, according to the report.
Zang was best known in Shanghai for his connection with the terrorist society once headquartered in the New Asia Hotel and known as the “Kingly Way Society.”
His connection with the group was discovered on the eve of August 13, 1938, when three of his henchmen were nabbed as they attempted to cross the Szechuen Road bridge to enter the International Settlement for a bombing raid on a number of Chinese schools.
A wanted notice with a reward attached was subsequently posted for Zang’s arrest by the police and he left town for parts along the Yangtse River. After a brief sojourn in Hankow, he traveled back to Nanking where he is said to have held some sort of a political job.
This is not the first time that news of his death has trickled into Shanghai. Zang is reported to have been killed on several other occasions, but denials, somewhat belated, have always been forthcoming.

“王道”
领袖据称
被暗杀

“两吨”常在宴会上
被击毙，
上海获悉

“两吨”常玉清，这位前苏州河以北地区本地恐怖团伙的头目，据称已死亡。
昨日本地半官方渠道收到的消息称，“两吨”三天前在南京被刺客枪杀。
据说有七名刺客闯入了常在南京举办的宴会。
军用毛瑟枪开始喷吐死亡，当硝烟散去时，“两吨”倒在地上，成为此次事件的主要伤亡者。据报道，“两吨”当场死亡。
常在上海最为人所知的是他与曾总部设在新亚酒店、被称为“王道社”的恐怖社团的联系。
他与该团体的联系在1938年8月13日前夕被发现，当时他的三名手下在试图穿过四川路桥进入公共租界对多所中国学校进行炸弹袭击时被抓获。
随后警方张贴了附有赏金的通缉令逮捕常，他离开上海前往长江沿线地区。在汉口短暂停留后，他返回南京，据说在那里担任某种政治职务。
这并非他的死讯第一次传入上海。据报道，常在其他几次场合也被传死亡，但总是会有迟来的否认。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

AUG 18 1939

CHINESE GANGSTER
SHOT IN NANKING

Zang Was Well-known To
Local Police And
Wanted Here

The long hand of retribution final-
ly smote Zang Yu-ching, a well-
known figure in Shanghai's Chinese
gangdom, when he was shot and
fatally wounded by seven Chinese
terrorists in Nanking on August 12,
according to a Chinese report yes-
terday.

Zang, who had successfully evad-
ed the International Settlement
police authorities who had issued a
warrant for his arrest in connection
with a series of crimes committed
in the Settlement areas, was former-
ly a public bath-house keeper in the
Sinja District. He figured promin-
ently as Chairman of the "Yellow
Way Society," which had had a
brief existence.

While passing through a street in
Nanking on August 12, seven
Chinese fired simultaneously at him,
fatally wounding him, according to
the report. His body-guard retaliat-
ed, and the seven Chinese terrorists
were reported to have either been
wounded or killed.

1939年8月18日

中国帮派分子
在南京被枪击

常为本地警方熟知
且在此地被通缉

据昨日一份中文报道，上海华人黑帮中的知名人物常玉清终于遭到报应，于8月12日在南京被七名中国恐怖分子枪击并受致命伤。

常此前成功躲避了公共租界警方的追捕，警方曾因其在租界地区犯下的一系列罪行发出逮捕令。他曾是新闸区的一家公共浴室老板。他曾作为短暂存在的“黄道社”主席而崭露头角。

据报道，8月12日，当他在南京的一条街道上经过时，七名中国人同时向他开枪，致其重伤。他的保镖进行了还击，据报道这七名中国恐怖分子非死即伤。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

AUG 18 1939

Notorious Gang
Leader Dead
"Two Ton Zang" Reported
To Have Been Murdered
In Nanking

Zang Yu-ching, better known as
"Two Ton Zang," the burly ex-butch-
er and pro-Japanese gangster, former-
ly operating from the New Asia Hotel
in Hongkew, who is wanted by the
Settlement police for many bombings
and shootings in Shanghai after the
conclusion of the hostilities, is report-
ed to be dead. Quoting a recent ar-
rival from Nanking, a Chinese news
agency reports that he was killed by
seven Chinese gunmen in Nanking
on the eve of the August 13 Incident.

The killing in Nanking has been
kept secret by both the Japanese and
Chinese officials in the former capital
but the report asserts that the seven
gunmen, who made the attack, were
also killed. They had a fight with
Zang's bodyguards and were all shot
and killed. Although details are not
available the Nanking arrival was
sure of the death of Zang.

It will be recalled that many ter-
rorists under Zang's direction have
been sentenced by the First Special
District Court to heavy prison terms.
Their targets of attacks were mostly
Chungking organizations and pro-
Chungking newspaper offices and
broadcasting stations and individuals.
When they appeared in court, the
terrorists confessed very frankly that
they were directed by Zang who
maintained headquarters in the
Hongkew hotel. They received wages
for doing the terrorist work and they
were punished in case they failed in
carrying out their missions.

The Settlement police then issued
a warrant for Zang's arrest but he
fled to Nanking where he was re-
ported to have organized another
gang. Some months ago, he was re-
ported to have come to Shanghai
once in order to get more "students."

Since then he has not been heard of.
The former butcher and bath house
manager weighed more than 300 lb.
and was for a time the most power-
ful Chinese in Shanghai soon after
the withdrawal of Chinese officials
and troops.

《华北每日新闻》。

1939年8月18日

臭名昭著的帮派
头目死亡
“两吨常”据报
在南京被谋杀

常玉清，更广为人知的名字是“两吨常”，这位魁梧的前屠夫兼亲日帮派分子，此前以虹口新亚酒店为据点活动，战事结束后因在上海制造多起爆炸和枪击案而被租界警方通缉，据报已死亡。一家中文通讯社引用一位近期从南京抵达的人士的话称，他在八一三事变前夕于南京被七名中国枪手杀害。

南京的这起杀人事件被前首都的日本和中国官员保密，但该报道声称，发动袭击的七名枪手也被杀害。他们与常的保镖发生交火，全部被枪杀。虽然细节不详，但这位从南京来的人确信常已死亡。

回想起来，许多在常指挥下的恐怖分子已被第一特区法院判处重刑。他们的攻击目标主要是重庆方面的组织、亲重庆的报社和广播电台以及个人。当他们在法庭上出现时，恐怖分子非常坦率地承认他们是受常指挥的，常的总部设在虹口的一家酒店。他们因从事恐怖工作而领取工资，如果未能完成任务则会受到惩罚。

随后租界警方发出了对常的逮捕令，但他逃往南京，据报在那里组织了另一个帮派。几个月前，据报他曾回到上海一次，以招募更多的“学生”。

此后便杳无音信。这位前屠夫兼浴室经理体重超过300磅，在中国官员和军队撤离后的一段时间内，曾是上海最有势力的中国人。

Made by Det. L.Spt. Bennett Forwarded by

Sir,

The at sealed letter reference to activities of terrorists was received at Louza Station at 1.20p.m. 17-6-39, being addressed to Central Station, delivered by post, post marked 16-6-39.

Translation of letter:

Information has been obtained from reliable source that shameless traitors, after having obtained support from certain party will create several terrorized cases in the Settlement on the forenoon of 17-6-39 and they will first use the tea-room of the Sun Company as a back-ground. As it concerns the public safety, I hope that you will prevent such incidents in time.

(Signed) Secret informer.
16-6-39.

Detectives of Louza Station were detailed for observation in the Sun Company tea-room, Nanking and Yu Ya Ching Road Corner, nothing suspicious noted.

D.O."A" informed.

No untoward incident re terrorist activities occurred in Louza District during 17-6-39, a shooting occurred at about 9.45 p.m. 17-6-39 on Swatow Road near Yu Ya Ching Road Corner, when 5 persons were wounded, but this was due to gambling or money quarrel (F.I.R. 380/39 Louza).

Detectives and uniform Police have been detailed for duty at newspaper offices in Louza District.

从可靠来源获得情报，无耻的叛徒在获得某方支持后，将于1939年6月17日上午在租界制造几起恐怖案件，他们将首先以先施公司茶室为背景。鉴于此事关乎公共安全，希望你们能及时阻止此类事件发生。

With reference to the attached information

on the movements of Chang Yu Ching, better known as
ZANG NGOH TSING of the "Hwang Tao" Association, I
have to report that the following information is in

In view of the forthcoming visit to Shanghai
of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, ex-Deputy Executive of the
Kuomintang, Mr. Liang Hung-chi, President of the
Administrative Yuan of the Reformed Government, is
greatly perturbed, as there is a possibility that
his official status will be then changed. Accord-
ingly a secret conference of various prominent govern-
ment officials was convened at Nanking, at which it
was decided to instruct Zang Ngoh-tsing to despatch
certain of his adherents to impersonate national
salvation elements and to assassinate Wang Ching Wei
should an opportunity arise. Should this mission be
successfully carried out, Zang will receive a reward
of $30,000.

Zang Ngoh-tsing, however, has no intention
of accepting the above-mentioned offer and on May 10,
in company with a Japanese Officer named Ohada, left
for Dairen, presumably on board the S.S. "Tsingtao
Maru".

On arrival at Tsingtao, Zang went ashore and
had a brief discussion over the organisation of branch

报 告
- - - - - -

关于附上的来自大学出版有限公司（University Press Ltd.）桑德斯-贝茨先生（Mr. Sanders-Bates）的情报，涉及以“黄道会”闻名的常玉清（ZANG NGOH TSING）的行踪，本人须报告称，我方掌握以下信息，但尚未得到证实。

鉴于国民党前执行委员汪精卫先生即将访问上海，维新政府行政院院长梁鸿志先生深感不安，因为其官方地位届时可能发生变更。因此，南京召开了一次由各重要政府官员参加的秘密会议，会上决定指令常玉清派遣其部分追随者冒充救国分子，并在有机会时刺杀汪精卫。如果此任务成功执行，常将获得30,000美元的赏金。

然而，常玉清无意接受上述提议，并于5月10日与一名名为 Ohada 的日本军官一同离开前往大连，据信是乘坐“青岛丸”号轮船（S.S. "Tsingtao Maru"）。

was ordered by the Japanes authorities to return

known, and that preparations for his welcome were
provided for by Zao Seeng-dao ( 趙 松 濤 ),
and other prominent members of the An Ching League
in Hongkew District.

Zang Ngoh-tsing is reported to have returned
to Shanghai for the purpose of assuming the post of
Commander-in-Charge of a "Storming Corps", a new
organisation of the Japanese Military, for sabotage
work in the Foreign Settlements.

May 24, 1939.

Dear Bourne,

Sanders-Bates of the University Press Ltd
telephoned our Bates confidentially this morning
that he had the following reports :-
(1) A movement was on foot to conduct acts of
sabotage on British property.
(2) As part of (1) a fire would be arranged in a near
enough to affect our Gough Island installation.
(3) A pro-Jap. terrorist named Chang Yu Ching
(spelling uncertain) had recently returned to
Shanghai from Dairen.

We have reported (1) and (2) to H.B.M. C.G.
and they are taking it up with the Japs but you may
be interested in (3). I have of course no idea upon
what Sanders-Bates bases his advice to us but if by
chance you know anything likely to confirm (3) it
might provide interesting confirmation of the threat
to our installation.

Yours sincerely,

T.S. Powell.

China Evening News of March 5 published the following comment:-

ARRIVAL OF ZANG NYOH-TSING IN SHANGHAI

By using threats, a certain party is attempting
to seize the Police rights in the International Settlement,
but the plot was detected by the British authorities. We
feel that the reply given by Britain is logical and proper.
As all the miscreants responsible for breaches of peace
and order in the Settlement are hiding in the suburbs of
the Settlement, the blame for such disturbances of peace
and order in the Settlement should be laid on the shoulders
of that party.

We should wait and see whether this party,
after the failure of its intrigue, will employ other vile
tricks to intensify the atmosphere of terrorism in the
Settlement and use it as a pretext for its ends.
There is a report that the 315-lb former
bath-house proprietor called Zang Nyoh-tsing (常玉清),
the head of the "Huang Dao Association" (黄道会) which
has been responsible for many terroristic activities in
the Settlement in the past, has arrived in Shanghai. He
may make a second attempt to disturb peace and order in
the Settlement.
The attempt on the life of a traitor at Zay
Hwa Feng (瑞华坊), French Concession, seems to us to be
a deliberate attempt to obscure the situation. The
bombing outrages on Nanking Road and the handbills
addressed to dance hall patrons seem to be a part of the
plot.
With the arrival in Shanghai of Zang Nyoh-
tsing, peace and order in the Settlement will not be safe.
Great Britain and the S.M.C. should maintain a firmer
stand; the entire community will support them.

3月5日的《China Evening News》刊登了如下评论：

常玉清抵沪

某方企图通过威胁手段夺取国际租界的警务权，但该阴谋已被英国当局识破。我们认为英国的回应合乎逻辑且得当。由于所有应对租界内破坏和平秩序行为负责的歹徒均藏匿于租界郊区，此类扰乱租界和平秩序的责任应归咎于该方。

我们应拭目以待，看该方在阴谋失败后，是否会采用其他卑劣伎俩加剧租界内的恐怖气氛，并以此作为实现其目的的借口。
有报告称，曾对租界过去许多恐怖活动负责的“黄道会”（黄道会）头目、前浴室老板、体重315磅的常玉清（常玉清）已抵达上海。他可能会再次企图扰乱租界的和平与秩序。
法租界瑞华坊（Zay Hwa Feng）发生的一起针对汉奸的未遂暗杀事件，在我们看来似乎是故意混淆视听之举。南京路上的爆炸暴行以及致舞厅顾客的宣传单，似乎也是该阴谋的一部分。
随着常玉清抵沪，租界的和平与安全将不再有保障。英国和上海公共租界工部局应采取更坚定的立场；整个社区都将支持他们。

extensive enquiries reveal that Zang is meantime in

return to Nanking before the end of the Chinese lunar
year (February 18). His present visit to Shanghai,

inaugurating a Kiangsu Branch and a Chekiang Branch in

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 24 1939

Corpulent “Yellow Way” Gang
Leader Organizes New Party

Shrine Opened In Nanking To Lure Elements
Of “Ching Pang” To Join Pro-Japanese
Group; Branches Established

His “Yellow Way Society” dissolved when things got too hot for him in Shanghai, the corpulent 250-pound Zang Yu-ching, notorious pro-Japanese gangster, is now trying to organize a “Green Circle Society” or “Anching Hwei” with branches in important railway towns in Kiangsu and Che-kiang, according to Chinese reports today.

Aimed to win over the undesirable elements from the “Ching Pang”, or the Green Circles, the images of the founders of this gang were placed in a shrine housed in the former office of the Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission in Nanking. Early last month Zang was reported to have come to Shanghai again. Hiding himself in the Western Area, he was said to have approached members of the Green Circle and urged them to join the “Anching League”, but many turned down his overtures.

Realizing that Hangchow is the birthplace of the Green Circle the pro-Japanese gangster leader, it is stated, recently went to the Lakeside City for the purpose of organizing a branch of the “Anching League”. Wang Jul-kai,

“Governor of Chekiang” is reported to have been asked to head the Hangchow branch.

It is further reported that Zang has sent his trusted followers to Soochow, Changchow, Kingtan, Tanyang, Yangchow and other towns on the Nanking-Shanghai and Shanghai-Hangchow Railways to organize branches of the “Anching League”.

The reports also declared that Zang recently sneaked back to Shanghai to make contacts with his Japanese employers. He left hurriedly, however, in view of the warrant for his arrest issued by the First Special District Court at the request of the Settlement police. He is understood to be wanted as the director of the terroristic activities inside the Settlement.

1939年1月24日

肥胖的“黄道”帮头目组织新党派

在南京设立神龛以引诱“青帮”分子加入亲日团体；已建立分支机构

据今日中文报道，这位体重250磅、臭名昭著的亲日帮派分子臧玉清（Zang Yu-ching），在其“黄道会”因在上海处境过于危险而解散后，现正试图组织一个名为“安清会”或“安清会”（Anching Hwei）的组织，并在江苏和浙江的重要铁路城镇设立分支机构。

旨在从“青帮”（Green Circles）中拉拢不良分子，该帮派创始人的画像被供奉在南京原蒙藏委员会办公室内的神龛中。据报道，臧于上月初再次来到上海。他藏身于西区，据说曾接触青帮成员，敦促他们加入“安清联盟”，但许多人拒绝了他的拉拢。

据悉，这位亲日帮派头目意识到杭州是青帮的发源地，最近前往这座湖滨城市，目的是组织“安清联盟”的一个分支。据报道，“浙江省主席”王鞠凯（Wang Jul-kai，音译）被邀请主持杭州分支。

另有报道称，臧已派遣其亲信前往苏州、常州、金坛（Kingtan，音译）、丹阳、扬州以及宁沪铁路和沪杭铁路沿线的其他城镇，以组织“安清联盟”的分支机构。

报道还称，臧最近潜回上海与其日本主子取得联系。然而，鉴于租界警方请求第一特区地方法院签发了逮捕令，他匆忙离开。据了解，他因被指为租界内恐怖活动的指挥者而受到通缉。

The League has its headquarters in Nanking and branches at various large cities throughout Central China. The Shanghai Branch, which is situated at House 31/1136, Yu Yuen Road, is in charge of Fu Sao Tong (傅少棠) and Zao Van Nyi (趙万義), both being well known loafers in the Gordon and Pootoo Road districts. December 7, 1938.
NIPPO

INAUGURATION OF AN CHING LEAGUE

As previously arranged, the
inauguration of the An Ching League took place at a certain
place in the International Settlement at 2.30 p.m. December 6.
About 300 persons representing the Green Pang attended the
inauguration, besides a number of honoured guests and
visitors. An altar was prepared under a Japanese flag and
five barred flag on the second floor for the founder of the
League.

All members of the League
solemnly took an oath standing in front of the altar in
the midst of rising smoke of burning incense and they made
three most respectful bows towards the altar.

Mr. Wu Hsien's report on the
history of the League was followed by speeches made by Mr.
Zang Nyoh Tsing, Chairman of Committee, Mr. Zang Tien Yui,
one of the honoured guests, and Mr. Li Ko Wei, one of the
visitors. The function ended with cheering for peace
in the Orient, the Imperial Government of Japan, the
Republic of China, the "Reformed Government" and the An
Ching League.

A lengthy manifesto on its
inauguration has been issued by the League.

Certified true copy.

December 7, 1938.

NIPPO

INAUGURATION OF AN CHING LEAGUE

As previously arranged, the
inauguration of the An Ching League took place at a certain
place in the International Settlement at 2.30 p.m. December 6.
About 300 persons representing the Green Pang attended the
inauguration, besides a number of honoured guests and
visitors. An altar was prepared under a Japanese flag and
five barred flag on the second floor for the founder of the
League.

All members of the League
solemnly took an oath standing in front of the altar in
the midst of rising smoke of burning incense and then made
three most respectful bows towards the altar.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 8 DEC. 1938 / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

Mr. Wu Hsien's report on the
history of the League was followed by speeches made by Mr.
Zang Nyoh Tsing, Chairman of Committee, Mr. Zang Tien Yui,
one of the honoured guests, and Mr. Li Ko Nei, one of the
visitors. The function ended with cheering for peace
in the Orient, the Imperial Government of Japan, the
Republic of China, the "Reformed Government" and the An
Ching League.

A lengthy manifesto on its
inauguration has been issued by the League.

Date November 18, 1938.
Subject Removal of the Huang Dao Association to Nanking
- Renamed as the An Tsing League (安清同盟)
Made by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With a view to effecting a closer relationship with
the different gangs of loafers in the interior similar in
character to themselves, the headquarters of the East Asia
Huang Dao Association, hitherto situated in the New Asia
Hotel, was removed to Nanking at the end of October 1938.
Subsequent to their removal, preparations were underway for
its reorganization and the renaming of the association as
the An Tsing Religion (literally the Safe and Pure Religion),
but before these arrangements had been completed, joint
instructions were issued by the Ministry of Interior of the
Reformed Government and the Special Service Section of the
Japanese Army, to rename the Association as the An Tsing
League. Zang Ngoh-tsing (常之清), formerly chief
of the Association, still acts as head of the League, and
has recently been appointed to the concurrent post of
Councillor of the Reformed Government, and is understood
to have a following of 2,000 in Nanking alone. A circular
notice was issued by the League headquarters instructing
the members of the former Huang Dao Association in different
localities to effect registration which commenced on
November 15, 1938 and is to be concluded seven days from
that date.

In Shanghai, an office of the former Huang Dao
Association is still maintained at 86, Moo Loo Jao, off
Field Road, O.O.L., under the name of the Special
Service Corps of the Ministry of Pacification of the
Reformed Government (維新政府綏靖部特務隊).

主题 黄道会迁往南京
- 更名为安清同盟 (An Tsing League)
制作人/及转呈人 克劳福德 (Crawford) 侦探督察

为了与内地性质相似的各种流氓帮派建立更紧密的关系，东亚黄道会总部此前位于新亚酒店，于1938年10月底迁往南京。搬迁后，重组工作随即展开，并将协会更名为安清教（字面意为平安纯洁之教），但在这些安排完成之前，维新政府内政部与日军特务科联合发出指令，将该协会更名为安清联盟。该协会前首领常之清 (Zang Ngoh-tsing) 仍担任联盟首领，最近被兼任维新政府参议，据悉仅在南京就有2000名追随者。联盟总部发布通函，通知各地前黄道会成员进行登记，登记工作于1938年11月15日开始，并于七天后结束。

在上海，前黄道会的一个办事处仍维持在界外地区斐伦路 (Field Road) 慕尔照 (Moo Loo Jao) 86号，名义为维新政府绥靖部特务队。
